workflows.name: sw-life-cycle
workflows.description: Full software life cycle for WingFoil UI: from WingFoil initialisation and product inception, through technical specification downcast, iterative per-release delivery, to end-of-life.

phases.name: init
phases.description: Initialize the WingFoil configuration (DNA, Memory schema, Directives, Workflows).

phases.name: inception
phases.description: Product discovery (Lean Inception) — produces the Vision Package.

phases.name: specification
phases.description: Downcast the vision into engineering specs (USM -> BDD -> SARD -> backlog).

phases.name: seed-first-release-line
phases.description: Create the first release-line (v1) so release-line-cycle has something to iterate.

phases.name: release-line-cycle
phases.description: Iterative delivery per major version — approve scope, generate its roadmap + initial ADRs/ DLs/tech-specs, run one release-cycle per minor release, then close it and self-seed the next release-line (if planned).

phases.name: sunset
phases.description: Retire the product / a major line at end of life.

workflows.name: bug-ingest
workflows.description: Capture a single defect report (bug) into Memory.

phases.name: capture
phases.description: Record the bug (summary, reproduction steps, severity).

phases.name: triage
phases.description: Triage and accept the bug for work (approval gate; reject = back to capture).

workflows.name: decision-log-ingest
workflows.description: Capture a single product/process decision (decision-log) into Memory.

phases.name: capture
phases.description: Record the decision (context, decision, rationale).

phases.name: approve
phases.description: Approve the decision (approval gate; reject = back to capture).

workflows.name: adr-ingest
workflows.description: Capture a single Architectural Decision Record (ADR) into Memory.

phases.name: capture
phases.description: Record the ADR (context, decision, consequences) and the SARD requirement(s) it implements.

phases.name: approve
phases.description: Accept the ADR (approval gate; reject = back to capture for revision).

workflows.name: service-ingest
workflows.description: Record a single external service (account, credential by reference, listing, setting, domain, handle) into Memory.

phases.name: capture
phases.description: Record the service (purpose, configuration, verification, management) with public identifiers only — never a secret value (dl-088 security rule, REQ-SEC-08).

post: secret-scan.clean: spec-007 scanText reports no blocking finding in the element (REQ-SEC-08)

phases.name: approve
phases.description: The approver runs the element's `verify` and confirms the description holds (approval gate; reject = back to capture).

workflows.name: wingfoil-init
workflows.description: Initialize the WingFoil configuration: DNA, Memory schema, Directives, Workflows.

phases.name: init-config
phases.description: Create the WingFoil configuration files (dna.yaml, memory.yaml, directives/, workflows.yaml).

workflows.name: lean-inception
workflows.description: Product discovery via Lean Inception. Five sessions transform the Product Brief into the Vision Package (vision, is/is-not, personas, journeys, features, sequencer, MVP canvas).

phases.name: vision
phases.description: Session 1 — Product Vision + Is/Is Not/Does/Does Not.

phases.name: personas
phases.description: Session 2 — Personas.

phases.name: journeys
phases.description: Session 3 — User Journeys.

phases.name: features
phases.description: Session 4 — Feature Brainstorm + Technical/Business Review.

phases.name: sequencer
phases.description: Session 5 — Sequencer + MVP Canvas.

workflows.name: specification-downcast
workflows.description: Downcast the strategic vision into actionable engineering requirements: User Story Mapping -> Specification by Example (BDD) -> Volere Requirements (SARD) -> backlog.

phases.name: user-story-mapping
phases.description: Module 1 — explode journeys into atomic stories; extract MVP.

post: 100% of MVP Canvas features covered; edge-case stories present

phases.name: specification-by-examples
phases.description: Module 2 — translate MVP stories into Gherkin BDD scenarios.

post: each scenario atomic + testable; zero ambiguous adjectives/adverbs

phases.name: volere-requirements
phases.description: Module 3 — extract architectural/NFR requirements (SARD, Volere shell).

post: every REQ has a numeric/percentage/boolean Fit Criterion

phases.name: backlog-export
phases.description: Module 4 — consolidate the chain into a structured operational backlog.

post: valid JSON; no duplicate IDs; no circular dependencies

workflows.name: user-story-mapping
workflows.description: Explode the macro-flows of Lean Inception into atomic, value-oriented user stories; build the backbone (horizontal axis), vertically explode functionalities, apply the MVP cut.

phases.name: backbone
phases.description: Extract sequential user tasks from journeys to form the spine.

phases.name: vertical-explosion
phases.description: Under each backbone step, write `As <persona>, I want <action> so that <benefit>`.

phases.name: mvp-cut
phases.description: Tag stories [MVP · vX] / [Future] using the sequencer.

post: 100% of MVP Canvas features included; edge-case stories generated

workflows.name: specification-by-examples
workflows.description: Translate MVP user stories into deterministic Gherkin scenarios (Given-When-Then), eliminating interpretive ambiguity. One happy path + one edge/error path per story.

phases.name: isolate-mvp
phases.description: Select only [MVP] user stories.

phases.name: write-scenarios
phases.description: For each story write Gherkin scenarios with concrete examples.

post: each story has >=1 happy path and >=1 edge/error path

workflows.name: volere-requirements
workflows.description: Extract and formalize infrastructure, business rules, and NFRs into the SARD using the Volere Requirement Shell (Description, Rationale, Traceability, Fit Criterion), grouped by macro-area.

phases.name: extract-requirements
phases.description: From BDD scenarios, extract the infrastructural requirements that support them.

phases.name: apply-volere-shell
phases.description: Structure each REQ: Description, Rationale, Traceability, Fit Criterion.

phases.name: group-by-macro-area
phases.description: Organize into: Architectural Constraints; Performance & Latency; State & Context; Integrations & Interfaces; Security, Roles & Governance.

post: every REQ has a clearly numeric, percentage-based, or boolean Fit Criterion

workflows.name: backlog-export
workflows.description: Consolidate the documentary chain (USM + BDD + SARD) into a single structured backlog, ready to sync into dev tools; partition tasks by release wave.

phases.name: generate-records
phases.description: One JSON record per MVP user story; Gherkin -> acceptance_criteria; one Technical Task per REQ.

phases.name: map-dependencies
phases.description: Link technical-task IDs into the dependencies[] of affected user stories.

phases.name: validate
phases.description: JSON Schema validation + partition by-release.

workflows.name: initial-design
workflows.description: Generate this release-line's minor-release roadmap, then record the initial Architectural Decision Records, Decision Logs, and Technical Specifications that formalize choices already implied by it — before this release-line's delivery begins.

phases.name: seed-releases
phases.description: Generate the RELEASE Memory files (the roadmap) for this release-line, that delivery iterates over.

post: frontmatter.required: [title, kind, version, pillar, features, requirements, release-line]

phases.name: seed-adrs
phases.description: Optionally record the initial Architectural Decision Records for this release-line.

phases.name: seed-dls
phases.description: Optionally record the initial Decision Logs capturing product/process choices behind this release-line.

phases.name: seed-specs
phases.description: Survey this whole release-line (not one release) for shared file formats, schemas, constant sets, and module APIs already implied by its roadmap + the config; scaffold a tech-spec for each one not yet covered by an approved spec.

workflows.name: release-line-cycle
workflows.description: Deliver one release-line end to end: approve its scope -> initial-design (roadmap + ADRs/DLs/ tech-specs) -> one release-cycle per minor release -> close it and seed the next release-line.

phases.name: approve
phases.description: Approve the release-line's scope so initial-design and delivery can begin.

phases.name: initial-design
phases.description: Generate this release-line's minor-release roadmap and record its initial ADRs/DLs/tech-specs.

phases.name: delivery
phases.description: Run one release-cycle per minor release belonging to this release-line.

phases.name: plan-next-release-line
phases.description: Once every release under this release-line is `released`: close this release-line, and — if another major version is planned — seed the next release-line (self-seeding: sw-life-cycle's own iterate_over: release-line will pick it up next).

pre: all releases where release-line={release-line.version} are status: released

workflows.name: release-cycle
workflows.description: Deliver one release: plan scope -> run a TDD dev-loop per backlog task (including bug-fix tasks) -> align user-facing docs -> submit -> publish to npm -> retrospective.

phases.name: planning
phases.description: Define release scope, story points, and the task backlog for this release.

phases.name: implementation
phases.description: Run the TDD dev-loop once per backlog task tagged for this release — including the fix tasks derived from bugs scheduled into this release; each keeps its source bug in sync (`bug.sync_state`, see dev-loop.yaml).

phases.name: user-docs
phases.description: Write/align README, user guide, CLI reference, examples, and CHANGELOG to the shipped surface before the release is assembled. Hard release blocker (dl-013).

phases.name: e2e-smoke
phases.description: Run a real `wingfoil init` + drive the CLI surface, asserting exit codes + schema-valid scaffolded artifacts, before the release is assembled.

phases.name: submit
phases.description: Assemble the release, run checks, request approval.

phases.name: publishing
phases.description: Tag, build, and publish to npm; mark the release released.

phases.name: retrospective
phases.description: Capture learnings and adjust the next release.

workflows.name: release-planning
workflows.description: Plan a release: confirm the pillar focus and scope, triage bugs and reconcile accumulated governance into their gated states, identify and spec shared artefacts up front, pull backlog tasks for the release, and stamp each included element with its `release`. Set the release element to `planning` then `in-development`.

phases.name: advance-pinned-build
phases.description: Before the release is planned, move the WingFoil build that governs this repository (the `wingfoil` devDependency pinned exactly in package.json) to the newest PUBLISHED version, if it is newer. Rule (dl-095 Q3): the pin moves forward only, never backwards, and only to a published build; every switch is its own commit changing only package.json and package-lock.json (`npm install --save-dev --save-exact wingfoil@X.Y.Z`), noted in the active phase plan. After a switch, re-run the CLI contract tests (spec-001; once they exist) and re-check the `wingfoil-cli` directive against the new build. On a defect that blocks a step: move to a published fix; if none exists, work by hand, record it in the plan and in the `wingfoil-cli` directive. The pin is the governance CLI only; the versions the UI supports for observed projects are the contract-test matrix (adr-001 D3/D4), advanced separately.

pre: `npm run -s wingfoil -- --version` == the version package.json pins (the build in use is the pinned one)
post: new pin >= old pin, and `npm view wingfoil versions` lists it (forward only, published only)
the switch commit changes only package.json and package-lock.json
`npm run -s wingfoil -- directives list` reports "warnings": []; CLI contract tests pass (when they exist)

phases.name: define-scope
phases.description: Confirm pillar focus + feature scope for the release (from the release Memory doc).

post: frontmatter.required: [title, kind, version, pillar, features, requirements, release-line]

phases.name: triage-bugs
phases.description: Select in-scope `open` bugs (selection filter: release empty or == {release in planning}) and triage them so downstream phases see only `triaged` bugs. Not-selected bugs are left untouched.

phases.name: reconcile-governance
phases.description: Sweep accumulated not-ready in-scope governance into its gated state so build-backlog/identify-specs never silently skip it. Idempotent — acts only on pre-gate elements (selection filter: release empty or == {release in planning}). Not-selected elements are left untouched.

phases.name: record-adrs
phases.description: Optionally record + approve Architectural Decision Records for this release's scope.

phases.name: identify-specs
phases.description: Survey the release scope for file formats, schemas, constant sets, and module APIs that will be implemented by this release's tasks; scaffold a tech-spec for each one not yet covered by an approved spec. Runs before tasks are created so build-backlog can reference approved (or at least pending) specs instead of discovering gaps task-by-task.

phases.name: build-backlog
phases.description: Create/triage task deliverables for the release, convert reconciled governance into tasks, and stamp the `release` assignment on every included element. For each in-scope `ready` DL, create the task(s) it implies (the DL STAYS `ready` — dl-017, no ready->in-develop). For each selected `triaged` bug, create one or more fix tasks (task.bug = the source bug's id) and schedule the bug into the release; from here the bug's own state tracks its derived task(s) automatically (dev-loop's `bug.sync_state`). Assignment (dl-016 §4): stamp `release = {release.version}` on every included decision-log, bug, tech-spec, adr, and task.

phases.name: commit-backlog
phases.description: Approve the planned tasks into the backlog so the dev-loop can pick them up, then move the release into development.

workflows.name: dev-loop
workflows.description: Test-first development loop for a single task: design -> red -> green -> refactor -> review. On review rejection, fall back to `red` and return the task to in-progress.

phases.name: start
phases.description: Pick up the task; create a feature branch; move it to in-progress.

phases.name: design
phases.description: Safety net for artefacts not caught by release-planning's `identify-specs`: verify that a tech-spec exists and is approved for every file format, schema, constant set, and module API the task will implement. No code is written until all relevant tech-spec elements are in approved state. For each still-missing spec: memory.add then memory.submit (draft -> pending).

phases.name: red
phases.description: Write a failing test that captures the task's acceptance criteria.

phases.name: green
phases.description: Implement the minimum code to make the test pass.

phases.name: refactor
phases.description: Refactor with tests green; keep coverage from regressing.

phases.name: review
phases.description: Quality gate runs the BDD acceptance tests, then the reviewer approves or rejects.

phases.name: done
phases.description: On approval, merge to main and mark the task done.

workflows.name: user-docs
workflows.description: Ensure the release's user-facing documentation is written and aligned before the release is assembled: README, user guide, CLI reference, working examples, CHANGELOG. Makes documentation a hard release blocker (dl-013) instead of an unenforced convention.

phases.name: check-implementation-complete
phases.description: Pre-check: every task tagged for this release is `done` before user docs are finalized.

pre: all tasks where tags=[{release.version}] are status: done

phases.name: align-user-docs
phases.description: Write/align the user-facing documentation to the shipped CLI/feature surface for this release.

post: user-facing docs aligned with the release's shipped CLI/feature surface

phases.name: align-agent-docs
phases.description: Verify and align the agent-facing entry point against the config it projects, so an agent's first contact describes the tool as it is. Runs after align-user-docs and before release-submit. Also reused by plan-next-release-line at release-line close (dl-025), because structural changes — a new Memory type, a changed state machine, a new pillar — land at release-line boundaries and are exactly what the element/state tables stop matching.

post: CLAUDE.md project status matches the shipped command surface (CORE_MODULES)

workflows.name: e2e-smoke
workflows.description: Black-box release gate: initialise a throwaway WingFoil project with the pinned CLI, start the WingFoil UI server on it, drive the screens in scope through a real browser, scan them for accessibility, and check that the packaged app launches. STAGED: warn on failure until the gate runs green for a release, then flip to hard-reject.

phases.name: fixture-project
phases.description: Create a throwaway git repository and run the pinned `wingfoil init` (each supported template), plus a few Memory elements in different states.
actions: cli.run("npm run -s wingfoil -- memory add ...; memory submit ...")

post: fixture covers every element state shown by the screens in scope

phases.name: drive-browser
phases.description: Start the server on the fixture project and drive the release's screens in a real browser (Playwright): read views render the fixture's state, and every gate action performed from the UI produces the same `wf(…)` commit the CLI would.

post: e2e suite passing on the supported browsers
every commit is a CLI wf(…) commit or a chore(ui) commit touching only .wingfoil/ui.yaml
actions refused on elements with local changes and while behind
fixtures: Kanban, custom, unknown types/states without ui.yaml; reviewer/product-owner with and without approver

phases.name: local-security
phases.description: Check the local server protections (X4): loopback only, session token, Origin/Host checks, no path outside the repository.

post: requests without the session token refused
Files refuses paths outside the repository

phases.name: accessibility
phases.description: Scan every screen in scope with axe-core and walk the keyboard path of each gate action.

post: every gate action reachable by keyboard

phases.name: contract
phases.description: Run the CLI JSON contract tests against the WingFoil versions the release supports (`wingfoil_min` .. pinned).

post: contract tests passing for every supported WingFoil version

phases.name: launch
phases.description: Install the packaged app as a user would (packaging decided at inception) and check it starts and serves the UI.

phases.name: gate
phases.description: Report smoke results. STAGED: warn on failure until the gate runs green for a release, then flip to hard-reject so it blocks release-submit.

post: e2e-smoke-passed (staged: warn until green for a release, then hard-reject)

workflows.name: release-submit
workflows.description: Assemble the release once its tasks are done: run pre-release checks, move the release into `releasing`, and gate on approval before publishing.

phases.name: pre-release-checks
phases.description: Verify all release tasks are done and the suite is green. Bugs have no independent status here — their state is derived by dev-loop's `bug.sync_state` from their fix tasks, so the task check below covers them; the bug check is a redundant sanity check on the sync itself.

pre: all tasks where tags=[{release.version}] are status: done
all bugs where tags=[{release.version}] are status: [resolved, closed]

phases.name: enter-releasing
phases.description: Move the release element into the releasing state.

phases.name: approve-release
phases.description: Final human approval before publishing.

workflows.name: release-publishing
workflows.description: Publish an approved release: tag, build, publish to the npm registry, and mark the release element as released.

phases.name: tag
phases.description: Create the semver git tag for the release ON `main`, after the release branch has merged — never on a phase branch (dl-024). The tag must be a stable ref reachable from main's permanent history so it survives phase-branch cleanup.

phases.name: publish
phases.description: Run the tag's publish pipeline, then make the staged version live. The tag push runs `.github/workflows/publish.yml`: gate, Verdaccio staging + dl-023 smoke, then promote, which STAGES the same tarball on npm with `npm stage publish` through the stage-only OIDC trusted publisher — no token (adr-011, spec-015 §3 stage 4). A staged version is not live: after the pipeline run, the approver inspects it (`npm stage view <stage-id>`) and approves it on npm with 2FA (`npm stage approve <stage-id>`, or Approve on npmjs.com), or discards it with `npm stage reject` (dl-087 Action 3). The runbook in publish.yml's header lists the one-time registry-side setup this step presupposes.

post: staged version approved on npm and live on the npm registry

phases.name: mark-released
phases.description: Mark the release element released.

workflows.name: retrospective
workflows.description: Close the release loop: EXPLORE the release's Execution Notes for friction, let the approver add points, capture what went well / what to improve as Memory, and feed adjustments into the next release planning.

phases.name: explore
phases.description: Mine the `## Execution Notes` of every Memory document in the release scope (tasks, bugs, DLs, the release doc, plan outcomes) for process friction — deviations, blockers, rejection reasons, honest-TDD notes, tooling gaps, inter-task dependency friction. Read-only; produces a structured, source-cited friction inventory grouped by theme. Parallelizable (cheap-model miners + synthesis).
produces: retrospective friction inventory (source-cited, grouped by theme)

phases.name: additional-points
phases.description: Approver gate: present the friction inventory + the identified improvement themes; the approver adds any further points to analyze (and, if a point implies a config/process change, a DL is spun off in capture). A review checkpoint, not an approval-gated transition — no commit.

phases.name: capture
phases.description: Record retrospective learnings as a Memory decision-log.

phases.name: approve
phases.description: Approve the retrospective so its actions are committed.

workflows.name: end-of-life
workflows.description: Retire the product (or a major line) at end of life: announce, deprecate active Memory and releases, and archive. Documents remain in the repo (agents ignore deprecated content).

phases.name: announce
phases.description: Record the end-of-life decision and timeline.

phases.name: deprecate
phases.description: Deprecate active releases and superseded ADRs / decision-logs.

post: deprecated content excluded from agent context and default search (REQ-STATE-06)

phases.name: archive
phases.description: Final commit; freeze the repository line.
